the design of a framework for automatic deployment of application-specific metadata and code in a middleware system.
the design and implementation of a middleware system that is self-managing, i.e., that is capable of automatically deploying application-specific functionality.

the design and implementation of a middleware system that can be easily administered and managed by a small team of developers and system administrators in a large scale distributed computing environment.

this work has demonstrated that the use of metadata-driven software tools to automate the deployment and maintenance of application-specific code and data types can greatly simplify the administration and management of large-scale distributed systems.

we have designed a framework that can be used by any middleware system to deploy application-specific functionality to a large scale system.

we have developed an infrastructure that allows a middleware system to be self-managed and self-administered.

a middleware system can be designed to be highly extensible and flexible without compromising performance.
the use of XML and Java technologies can significantly reduce the cost of managing and deploying application-specific metadata and code in middleware systems.
